note: Freshness schedule for every published package. Hand-maintained: cadence, next_due and note are judgement, not derived. last_retrieved is copied from the package's own data/metadata.json, taking the OLDEST sources[].retrieved, because a package is only as fresh as its stalest source; source mirrors sources[0] there and sources_count says how many it has. test/refresh-schedule.test.mjs holds the two in step, so a refresh that forgets this file fails the build instead of going stale quietly. cadence n/a means the package ships no data of its own (umbrella or code), manual means the source has no scripted path, and blocked means the fetcher must not be run until the reason in note is resolved. next_due is last_retrieved + cadence unless a note says otherwise; packages with cadence manual, blocked or n/a have none.

cadences.quarterly: refresh every three months; the default
cadences.semiannual: refresh every six months; high-volume sources whose review pass is the real cost
cadences.manual: no scripted path; refresh is a hand pass, scheduled per batch
cadences.blocked: do not run the fetcher until the reason in note is resolved
cadences.n/a: ships no data of its own

source.name: Yalidine Express: nos-agences

packages.note: Carded carriers (Anderson, Noest, Maystro, ZR Express, Swift Express, HHD Express) are re-geocoded on every run by resolving each agency's Google Maps link, so the fetcher holds what it already published whenever a run cannot better it: a card whose link does not resolve or carries no coordinate keeps its committed point and precision (pinFor), a card whose pin lands in a wilaya other than the one it declares is dropped, unless that wilaya was carved out of the declared one by the 2021 or 2026 reform (the parent comes from the flagship registry's mother_wilaya_code, never from a code range), with the card id, the declared wilaya and the resolved coordinate in the run log, rather than shipping last quarter's point as this run's, and a renamed card takes back the id it published if the new one lands within 100 m of it (carryRenamedIds), because a carded id is minted from the card title. An operator pin counts as verified however far it moves a desk. A Maps place linked by cid alone carries no coordinate, so those pins are committed with provenance in scripts/maps-cid-pins.json and used only as a fallback. Noest ids come from its stable card codes, so renames never move them. Every pull is committed under sources/livraison/ as a rights-safe projection of the rows the build consumes, plus a resolution cache for the carriers' Google Maps links, so `node scripts/fetch.mjs --cache` rebuilds the package from the store with no network at all and reproduces it byte for byte.

source.name: Direction Générale de la Protection Civile

packages.note: Already automated: the guarded scheduled promotion workflow (sources/README.md) refreshes the DGPC capture monthly and only promotes it when every gate passes. dgpc.dz drops TCP from outside Algeria (verified 2026-10-25, every A record, port 443), so a live pull needs an Algerian vantage point. The commune join is fixed: the DGPC's own commune_1 decides, across a spelling difference of up to two edits when exactly one commune of the wilaya is that close, and otherwise the commune whose OpenStreetMap outline contains the point decides before the nearest commune centre. Every clause reads the sources only. The 2026-10-25 replay of the stored capture landed with 18 units re-placed, and 23-017, whose DGPC name and containing outline disagree and which the sources cannot settle, is pinned to El Bouni by a reviewed row in quality/overrides/protection-civile.json.
